findings.state_artifact: tests/e2e/test-e2e-goal-4chantiers-wave-B.spec.js:311-389 (no PNG/console artifact -- this is a test-code defect found by reading the spec, not a rendered-page defect)
findings.evidence: The wave's OWN stated language (quoted in round-1 B-001's evidence) calls 'kiosk-stays-at-1-beep' one of the wave's TWO 'cannot fail' acceptance criteria. But the entire kiosk-regression block -- including both of its load-bearing assertions `expect(beepsAfterKiosk - beepsBeforeKiosk).toBe(1)` (line 385) and `expect(beepsSettled - beepsBeforeKiosk).toBe(1)` (line 386) -- is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (e) { console.warn(...) }` (try opens line 311, catch at line 388-389) that does NOT re-throw, does NOT call test.fail()/expect(false), and does NOT distinguish 'infra flake during seeding' from 'assertion genuinely violated'. Any future regression that makes a kiosk-origin order beep 2 or 3 times (the exact defect this test exists to catch, per its own docstring at the top of the file: 'a single 0.4s beep was inaudible... keep the single beep') would cause the `expect().toBe(1)` to throw, be swallowed by this catch, print only a Node-side console.warn (which -- ironically, the same class of bug as the original B-001 -- lands in Playwright's stdout, NOT in any .console.json artifact, since it is Node-side not page.evaluate-side), and the overall spec would still exit with status:'passed'. Verified this round's actual run did NOT hit this catch (07-kiosk-order-single-beep-regression.console.json's 'kiosk-regression' log shows deltaAfterSeed:1, deltaSettled:1, both assertions genuinely satisfied -- so the current behavior is correct), but the SAFETY NET for catching a future silent regression on this exact acceptance criterion does not exist: green today gives zero assurance for tomorrow. This try/catch predates round 2 (git diff b65cae50b..a92d5e232 shows the try/catch structure itself untouched; round 2 only added evidence-logging calls inside it), so it is not a round-2 regression, but it was not previously flagged by any reviewer and directly undermines the 'cannot fail' claim.
findings.fix_hint: Split the try/catch: keep seeding/network-wait failures (tinker() call, waitForResponse timeout) soft-failing with a warn (genuine environment flakiness), but move the two `expect(...).toBe(1)` calls OUTSIDE the catch's blast radius -- e.g. capture the seed/wait result in a variable, close the try block before the assertions, and let a genuine count mismatch throw uncaught so the spec fails red. Alternatively, wrap only the seed+wait in try/catch with an explicit `test.skip()` on infra failure, and always run the two assertions unconditionally afterward when a kiosk order was actually seeded.
